_comment: ADR-037 register fragment — buildiq-exports-flows-and-agents (kind: code). Adds the two exportJob properties ExportJobService::queue() has always WRITTEN but the schema never DECLARED: `flows` and `applicationSlug`. MEASURED, not inferred — OpenRegister stores only the properties a schema declares, and it does so SILENTLY: a POST to /api/objects/buildiq/export-job carrying `flows`, `applicationSlug` and a nonsense key echoed all three back in the 200 response, while an immediate fresh GET of the same object returned neither (only applicationUuid, applicationVersion, includeSeedData, license, status, target). So queue() wrote both, OR dropped both, RunExportJob::executePipeline() read them back absent, and nothing logged a word. Consequences, both live before this fragment: (1) `flows` — `is_array($job['flows'] ?? null)` was false on every job, so FlowAndAgentExportBundler::bundleFlows() returned immediately and NO bound flow was ever written into lib/Settings/flows/, while the export job still transitioned to `succeeded` and produced a downloadable ZIP; the e2e assertion 'the bound flow must be in the ZIP — this is the whole feature' (tests/e2e/export-flows-and-agents.spec.ts) is what caught it. (2) `applicationSlug` — RunExportJob:150 fell back to its `'exported-app'` default on EVERY export, so each exported app was scaffolded with appId/namespace/name `exported-app` instead of the real slug, and FlowAndAgentExportBundler::bundleAgents() queried agents whose `applicationSlug` is `exported-app`, matched none, and returned no skip — so agents were never exported either, silently. Both are declaration-only fixes: no PHP changes, because the writing and reading code was already correct. SettingsService::deepMergeConfig recurses into components.schemas.exportJob.properties and adds only these two keys — exportJob.required and every other exportJob property are untouched, and no other schema (incl. Application, which declares its own `flows` binding in 22-flows-and-agents.json) is touched. Both are OPTIONAL: every ExportJob record predating this fragment simply lacks them, which is what queue()'s `?? []` and RunExportJob's `?? 'exported-app'` already mean. ⚠️ The exportJob schema `version` in openbuild_register.json is bumped alongside this fragment: OpenRegister SKIPS the import when the deployed version is >= the declared one, so a property added without a bump deploys nowhere but a fresh install. See also PR #219, which bumps the same field for the same reason.

applicationSlug.title: Application Slug
applicationSlug.description: Slug of the source Application, captured at submission time by ExportJobService::queue() from the route parameter. RunExportJob reads it back to build the export context (appId, appNamespace, appName) and to resolve the agents that point at this application via `agent.applicationSlug`. Persisted on the job rather than re-derived from applicationUuid because the export runs as a background job, long after the request, and the slug is the identity the exported app is BUILT with: re-resolving it later would let a renamed Application change the appId of an export already in flight.

flows.title: Flows

flow.title: Flow UUID
flow.description: UUID of an OpenRegister flow named in the source Application's `flows` bindings, as chosen at export-submission time. Resolved by FlowAndAgentExportBundler against the OpenRegister `Flow` ENTITY (FlowMapper::findByUuid). The store the engine executes. And NOT against the `agentflow` object mirror, which drifts from it. A UUID and not the numeric `id`: an id is a per-instance auto-increment column and would resolve to a different flow, or to nothing, on the importing instance.

flows.description: Per-export choice of which of the source Application's `flows` bindings to bundle. Export-flow state persisted on the ExportJob record by ExportJobService::queue() (via sanitiseFlows(), which keeps only `flow` and drops the builder-UI `label`). Not Application configuration; the Application's own binding lives on Application.flows, declared in 22-flows-and-agents.json. Absent on every ExportJob created before this property existed; ExportJobService::queue() defaults it to [].
